title: Sparse concurrency efficiency annotated bench memo
body:
Purpose:
This note collects a compact set of microbenchmarks and annotated observations exploring how sparse concurrency (fractional slot occupancy, intentionally underfilled warps of work) interacts with cost-per-query and tail latency under realistic sessionized workloads. The goal is to produce a short, sharable artifact the Console and Optimize teams can use when recommending defaults for small-to-medium tenants.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Sparse concurrency (leaving some slot capacity intentionally empty to reduce contention) reduced p99 tail amplification in spikey session mixes by ~18–35% depending on shaping, with a CPU cost of ~2–6% higher (controller overhead) and GPU throughput loss of ~6–12% in sustained windows.
- For workloads dominated by short-chat-turns (mean tokens per request <= 60), sparse concurrency + small tiling (tile size 4–8) gives the best latency/cost tradeoff; for long-output generation workloads tiling helps less and quantization+kv-prefetch remain primary levers.

Experimental setup:
- Hardware: 8x A100 40GB hosts (multi-tenant worker pool), single region; MPS disabled for deterministic per-GPU isolation.
- Runtime: latest local branch from PR 486 (tiling + sparse-slot scheduler) with fixed kernel-selection table.
- Models: mix of an Llama-2-13B fp16 and quantized 13B-int8 variant (same architecture, different binaries).
- Workloads: three synthetic mixes derived from production traces: short-chat (80% <=60 tokens), mixed (50/50 short/long), long-form (avg 400 tokens). Bursts injected as Poisson arrivals with peak 8x baseline for 30s windows.
- Metrics collected: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency per request, cost proxy = GPU-ms * $/GPU-ms normalized per 1k queries, slot-utilization (fraction of occupied request-slots), preemptions, and KV cache hit rate.

Annotated numbers (representative slices):
NOTE: cost numbers are normalized to baseline (dense full packing, no tiling, Llama-2-13B fp16) where baseline cost=1.00. Latencies in ms.

Table: short-chat mix, burst window (30s peak), Llama-2-13B fp16
- Baseline (dense packing): p50=22 ms, p90=45 ms, p95=78 ms, p99=260 ms, cost=1.00, slot-util=0.98
- Sparse-concurrency (leave 20% slots empty): p50=23 ms, p90=41 ms, p95=62 ms, p99=195 ms, cost=1.06, slot-util=0.78
- Sparse + tiling (tile=6): p50=20 ms, p90=38 ms, p95=55 ms, p99=170 ms, cost=1.08, slot-util=0.74
- Sparse + tiling + int8 quant: p50=19 ms, p90=35 ms, p95=50 ms, p99=160 ms, cost=0.85, slot-util=0.70

Table: mixed workload, sustained window, quant vs fp16
- Baseline fp16: p50=35 ms, p90=82 ms, p95=140 ms, p99=380 ms, cost=1.00
- Sparse 15%: p50=36 ms, p90=74 ms, p95=120 ms, p99=300 ms, cost=1.04
- Quant-int8 baseline (dense): p50=31 ms, p90=68 ms, p95=110 ms, p99=240 ms, cost=0.78
- Quant + sparse 15%: p50=32 ms, p90=65 ms, p95=100 ms, p99=210 ms, cost=0.81

Observations and interpretation (bulleted):
- Tail improvement mechanism: leaving intentional slack reduces head-of-line blocking when large, long requests are scheduled concurrently; lower queueing variability -> p99 drops. The effect is strongest during short-turn dominated bursts when many independent small requests compete for aggregation.
- Cost trade: measured controller CPU cycles and slightly lower GPU packing efficiency explain the 4–10% cost delta on average. However quantization can offset and beat baseline unit cost while retaining tail benefits.
- Slot-util vs latency: a non-linear region exists. Above ~92% slot-util we see sharp p99 amplification; target operating point between 70–85% gives most of the latency benefit with modest cost overhead.
- KV cache: hit rates fell slightly (~2–4%) in very sparse regimes (slots empty -> fewer warm sessions per tile) which hurt long-form workloads; prefer sparse mostly for chatty short-turn apps.
- Tiling interactions: small tiles (4–8) reduce amplification of tail more than large tiles because they increase granularity of scheduling and avoid large-block packing inefficiencies.

ASCII sparkline sketches (p99 vs slot-util for short-chat burst):
- 60% |=====> p99=140ms
- 70% |=====> p99=170ms
- 80% |==========> p99=210ms
- 90% |=================> p99=310ms
- 98% |==============================> p99=520ms

Short-case recommendations (what to default to in Console presets):
- "Chat-responsive" preset: sparse_target=0.78 slot-util, tile_size=6, prefetch=on, quant_profile=optional-int8. Rationale: minimizes p99 with modest cost change; empirically best for short chat workloads.
- "Balanced" preset: sparse_target=0.85, tile_size=8, quant=none. Rationale: slightly higher utilization for cost-sensitive mixed workloads, still avoids p99 cliff.
- "Throughput-first" preset: sparse_target=0.92, tile_size=12, aggressive-packing. Rationale: maximize throughput; accept tail risk for batch-style backfills and long-form run generation.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Workload classification accuracy: need a lightweight estimator in the dataplane that labels tenant mix (short vs long) with >85% accuracy for automatic preset selection.
- Cross-tenant interactions: these tests used single-tenant pools. Multi-tenant fragmentation may change the optimal slot-util target; run multi-tenant synthetic experiments next sprint.
- KV cache tuning: measure cache warmth decay under sparse slot occupancy and explore session-affinity heuristics to preserve hit rate.

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- Data tables above are median-of-5 runs; variance between runs ~6–12% for p99 numbers depending on burst seed. Not polished; intended as sketch for Console UX and Optimize whitepaper.
- I left raw CSVs in: s3://redwood-bench/sparse-concurrency/sep12-2028/ (raw histograms + flame graphs)
- See linked PR for the scheduler implementation details.

Next steps (two-week plan):
1) Re-run mixed multi-tenant tests with two tenant classes (chatty vs long-form) and compare cross-tenant p99 leak; deadline: 2028-09-26.
2) Instrument lightweight dataplane classifier and run AB test selecting "Chat-responsive" vs "Balanced" on a small cohort; deadline: 2028-10-10.
3) Draft one-pager for Optimize recommending presets + cost math for customer-facing collateral; deadline: 2028-10-17.

Appendix: commands used (for reproducibility)
- run harness: ./bench/run_trace_mix.sh --trace short-chat --workers 128 --tiles 6 --sparse-target 0.78 --model llm13-fp16 --seed 42
- cost proxy calc: python tools/calc_cost.py --gpu-ms --pricing 0.00011 --normalize 1000

End of memo.
